title: quote has no error handling around the pricing call
rationale: If client.price rejects (pricing service down, unknown sku, timeout), quote has no try/catch, so the rejection propagates to the router with res never called; the failure path depends on unshown framework handling. A try/catch returning a 500 or not-found response would make the behavior explicit. Re-rated to nit because the consequence rests on how the unshown router handles rejections.

title: Receipt enqueued inside the transaction can run before commit and fail with RecordNotFound
rationale: deliver_later enqueues on a separate connection while the order's transaction is still open, so the job can run before the commit and read an Order that does not yet exist, raising RecordNotFound and dropping the receipt. The ReceiptMailer documentation explicitly requires enqueuing after commit, not inside the transaction block.

title: Full plaintext API key logged to audit log
rationale: The minted API key is written to the audit log in plaintext. The audit log is a persistent, likely replicated record, so anyone with log access obtains a credential that the rest of the system treats as stored-only-as-a-hash. This is a credential leak on a path that runs on every mint.

title: Query uses context.Background(), ignoring request cancellation
rationale: The query is bound to context.Background() rather than r.Context(), so it runs to completion even after the client disconnects, tying up a database connection for results nobody will read. Using r.Context() ties the query lifetime to the request.

title: Concurrent cache misses render the same page multiple times (cache stampede)
rationale: Concurrent requests for the same uncached slug each call p.Cache.Put and p.Render, so a burst on a cold or expired key performs the render once per request rather than once. If Render hits the database, a popular page expiring under load creates a thundering herd; this assumes Cache.Get/Put provide no single-flight behavior, which was not shown.

title: Get error is discarded, treating a cache failure the same as a miss
rationale: If Get returns an error for a backend failure rather than only a miss, the error is indistinguishable from a miss and every request falls through to Render and Put; if Put also fails, the page is re-rendered on every request with no signal. This rests on the unshown cache contract — it is only a real defect if Get can fail with a live backend.

title: total() double-converts a value that is already in cents
rationale: LineItem.priceCents is documented as an integer number of cents, but total() passes it through toCents, whose name implies conversion of a currency amount into cents. If toCents multiplies by 100 or rounds a fractional dollar amount, every total returned is wrong by orders of magnitude or by rounding, and that value is the amount actually charged. This rests on the assumption that toCents performs a multiplication; if it is a no-op or the field is actually dollars, the fix is to correct the naming and documentation instead.

title: Retry re-issues a charge that may already have succeeded
rationale: The docstring identifies timeouts after the processor received the request as the failure mode being retried. In that case the first charge may still succeed, so the retry can double-charge the customer unless `gateway.charge` deduplicates via an idempotency key, which the shown code does not establish.

title: New client (8 keep-alive sockets) created per request
rationale: `createClient` is documented as expensive and long-lived: one per process, shared. Creating a client per request opens eight keep-alive sockets that are never closed, exhausting file descriptors under load. Hoist the client to module scope and reuse it.

title: Receipt email is enqueued inside the transaction and can fire for a rolled-back or uncommitted order
rationale: deliver_later runs inside the open transaction: a worker that picks up the job before commit will not find the order, and if line_items.create! on line 10 raises, the email is still enqueued for an order that was never committed. Enqueue after the transaction block (or use an after_commit hook) so the receipt only goes out for a persisted order.

title: URLs derived from title lose per-post uniqueness
rationale: URLs are now derived from the title, so two posts with the same title collide on the same URL, and an existing post's URL changes when its title is edited and republished. This rests on the assumption that text.Slug does not guarantee uniqueness — its contract is not shown — but if it does not deduplicate, URL-based lookups can resolve to the wrong post.

title: Publish uses Slug without checking for an empty slug, producing the URL "/posts/"
rationale: Slug's documented contract requires callers to check for an empty result, and Publish does not: Publish(1, "???") returns the URL "/posts/", the bare collection URL. Every such post lands on the same page and the URL no longer identifies the post.

title: total() applies toCents to values that are already in cents, inflating totals 100×
rationale: LineItem.priceCents is documented as an integer number of cents, but total() passes it through toCents, which multiplies dollars by 100. A line of 1999 cents at quantity 1 yields 199900, so every computed total is 100× too large and the customer is charged the wrong amount.

title: Full API key written to SIEM audit log
rationale: The audit log ships verbatim off-host and its own documentation explicitly forbids passing credentials as fields. Logging the full API key writes a live secret to a seven-year, organisation-wide-readable store; the key id already identifies the minted key.

title: Cleanup passes an empty Filter to DeleteWhere, allowing bulk deletion of all uploads
rationale: Cleanup builds a Filter directly from optional query parameters and does not refuse an empty one, which DeleteWhere's contract requires callers to do. A request to DELETE /admin/uploads with no parameters matches every row and deletes every upload; a dropped or mis-constructed client request silently performs a full-table delete.

title: Query ignores request cancellation by using context.Background()
rationale: Using context.Background() means a client disconnecting mid-request does not cancel the underlying database query, so the store keeps serving an abandoned request's work. Passing r.Context() ties the query's lifetime to the request at no cost.

title: Retrying a non-idempotent card charge risks double-charging
rationale: `with_retry` documents that a timed-out request may already have been processed, and card charging is not safe to repeat. Since `settle` uses it to retry `gateway.charge`, a charge that succeeded but timed out can be issued again, double-charging the customer in violation of the documented idempotency requirement. The charge should carry an idempotency key (e.g. derived from the order), or `settle` should not retry timeouts.

title: Expired tokens are accepted as valid authentication
rationale: verify() deliberately returns claims for expired tokens, and its contract requires callers to check is_expired(claims) before trusting the result. current_user never does, so an expired but validly signed token authenticates the caller indefinitely — exactly the case the contract warns about.

title: Delay is divided by 1000, but schedule() expects milliseconds
rationale: schedule() takes its delay in milliseconds, so dividing parseDuration's millisecond result by 1000 makes every delayed job run 1000× too early: registerDelayed(job, "5m") fires after 300 ms. The doc comment stating the delay is converted to seconds documents the bug rather than the contract.

title: Re-uploading an existing filename silently destroys the previous file
rationale: save()'s documented contract requires callers to check exists() and refuse or rename whenever the path derives from a user-supplied filename. This call passes the client-controlled name straight through, so a second upload under the same name permanently destroys the earlier file while the client receives a 201 as if it were a fresh store.
